slides.headline: THESE 6 AI PROMPTS NEGOTIATE YOUR BILLS, RENT, AND SALARY IN SECONDS AND SAVE YOU UP TO $7,500 A YEAR
1) FIGHT ANY BILL IN 30 SECONDS
slides.body: A billing advocate costs $150/hour. Claude does this in 30 seconds "Here is my bill. Find every inflated charge and write me a firm dispute letter"

slides.headline: 2) CUT ANY SUBSCRIPTION PRICE BY 40%
slides.body: Companies would rather give you 40% off than lose you. They just need to hear you're leaving "Write an email to [service] saying I found a cheaper option and asking for a loyalty discount"

slides.headline: 3) NEGOTIATE YOUR WAY OUT OF ANY CONTRACT
slides.body: Most contracts hide cancellation rights in the fine print. AI reads every line you skipped "Here is my contract. Find every way I can cancel without a fee and write me a cancellation notice"

slides.headline: 4) TALK YOUR LANDLORD DOWN AT RENEWAL
slides.body: The average renter overpays $1,200/year because they never push back on increases "My rent is $X in [city]. Find 5 comparable listings nearby and write a polite renewal negotiation letter"

slides.headline: 5) NEVER OVERPAY FOR A CAR AGAIN
slides.body: The average buyer overpays by $2,000. Dealerships train for this. Now you can too "I want a [car]. Tell me the fair price, what tricks the dealer will use, and write me a script"

slides.headline: 6) COUNTER ANY JOB OFFER LIKE A PRO
slides.body: The average person leaves $7,500/year on the table by not negotiating their first offer "Here is my job offer for [role]. Research market rates and write a confident counter-offer email"

slides.headline: SAVE THIS FOR YOUR NEXT NEGOTIATION
slides.body: Bookmark these for your next bill, lease, or job offer. Daily AI prompts and real skills you can use tonight

hook_tournament.why: FIGHT YOUR BILLS hits like a punch — 'fight' is visceral and adversarial in a way 'negotiate' isn't, and bills are universally hated so it's instantly personal. The runner-up ('negotiate for you') is the same skeleton but the verb is too polished and corporate to make you feel anything at 2am.

hook_sharpen.why: "Feel like cheating" is a visceral emotional trigger — it implies unfair advantage and makes you need to know what the trick is, regardless of context. The runner-up [2] is more concrete but 'fight your bills' narrows the audience; 'cheating' hooks anyone who's ever negotiated anything.

editor_override: §2 HOOK — two actions joined by AND: 'NEGOTIATE… AND SAVE YOU UP TO $7,500.' Doctrine says one actor, one action; AND joining two actions = cut the weaker one.
